description: Real test of the pk/vk-caching split (cmd/setupkeys + cmd/provewith) added to the zk-m7 spike, run on the same AWS r7i.2xlarge tier-A used for docs/design/007-receipt-log-proof.md's §14.6. Confirms the design doc's implicit assumption -- that PLONK setup is separable from per-witness proving -- actually holds in this project's own gnark/AlgoPlonk pipeline, and measures the real marginal per-proof cost for the first time (previously only the full cold-pipeline cost, ~$0.30/proof, had been measured).

one_time_setup.Ptau: powersOfTau28_hez_final_26.ptau (reused, superset of the 2^24 tier A needs -- avoided a fresh 19GB download)
one_time_setup.notes: Ran once. These artifacts are then reused by cmd/provewith for every subsequent proof -- no compile, SRS load, Lagrange build, or Setup repeated.

marginal_proofs.cross_check: leaf_hash matches the value measured in the original full-pipeline tier A run exactly
a different real receipt, proved from the SAME cached keys with no setup repeated -- this is the actual point of the test

conclusion.ratio: 8.3x cheaper once the one-time setup is cached and reused
conclusion.caveat: Both proofs used the SAME instance that had just finished the one-time setup, so key-load read from a warm page cache -- a cold-boot spin-up-per-request architecture would add real instance-boot time (~1-2 min) on top of the 44-46s key-load measured here, not change the Prove step itself.
